title: Runtime token overrides for form components — theme handshake and validation layering
creator: Leah Martinez
description: Background: As more customers adopt tenant theming and runtime feature flags (Dedicated/Private), design tokens for form components (text fields, selects, toggles, validation states) are being overridden at runtime by platform code. Current token mappings assume static build-time tokens which leads to inconsistent validation contrast, label anchoring, and spacing when customers override primary/neutral surfaces or apply compact density. Goals: 1) Define a clear runtime token handshake between platform (engineers) and design (component semantics) so overrides preserve accessibility and spacing. 2) Introduce a small set of runtime-resilient tokens and defensive fallbacks for validation layers (error/soft/warning) and focus/hover states. 3) Provide a migration checklist and developer API examples so engineers can safely allow per-tenant token overrides without breaking form affordances. This ticket delivers the design spec, component guidance, and a staging checklist for engineering to implement a runtime token resolver with validation layering rules.
acceptance_criteria: A design spec exists that lists a minimal runtime token surface for form inputs (8–12 tokens) and their prioritized fallbacks.
Examples showing tenant overrides for dark and high-contrast themes with preserved validation contrast (WCAG AA minimum) are included.
Interaction guidance for label anchoring, autofill, and placeholder behavior under overridden color/token sets is documented.
A migration checklist for component owners and platform engineers with concrete code snippets demonstrating token resolution order is provided.
Design review & accessibility review signed off by Design Lead and Accessibility Engineer.
Links to mockups and a GitHub PR stub for the runtime resolver are attached.
design_notes: Surface token subset: surface-bg, surface-strong, surface-muted, text-primary, text-muted, interactive, border, focus-ring, error, warning, success, height-token (for density). Keep subset intentionally small to reduce runtime complexity.
Token semantics: tokens are semantic (e.g., surface-strong = input fill, border = outline color). Do not expose shadow/blur tokens to tenants.
Validation layering: error/warning/success tokens must map to a contrast ratio >= 3:1 against surface-bg and >= 4.5:1 for text-on-error where the message is inline.

Fallback strategy: when an override produces insufficient contrast, platform must automatically apply a lightness-adjusted fallback (algorithm recommended in spec). Design will produce a tone-adjusted step sequence for engineers.
Label anchoring: floating labels should use a separate token (label-floating) so that tenant overrides to surface colors do not reduce label contrast against the focused fill.

Density interactions: height-token ties to padding/line-height; runtime density overrides should be bounded to prevent overlap with icons/truncation. Recommend min height 32px for touch, 28px for compact.
Autofill resilience: define autofill overlay token and fallback so browser autofill color shifts don't break validation border visibility.
Performance: prefer numeric tokens for spacing and heights to avoid runtime CSS parsing costs; color tokens remain strings but keep count low.
migration_plan: Phase 0 — Prototype: provide a Figma theme with three tenant overrides (brand-light, brand-dark, high-contrast) and test the visual deltas against existing components.
Phase 1 — Token spec handoff: publish the runtime token doc and a short checklist for engineers (resolver order, contrast check, label-floating usage).
Phase 2 — Staging rollout: engineers implement resolver with a feature flag; design QA runs visual diff tests and spot-checks on selected customer themes.
Phase 3 — Gradual enablement: toggle runtime overrides for a small set of Dedicated customers, collect metrics on layout regressions and accessibility failures.
Phase 4 — Wide rollout: enable for all tenants and add to onboarding docs with example snippets for theme creators.
accessibility_considerations: All validation text must meet WCAG AA when displayed over any allowed surface-bg; provide a contrast-checking step in the resolver.
Keyboard/Focus: focus-ring token must be visible regardless of tenant border overrides; the resolver should escalate to a high-visibility ring if border contrast drops below threshold.
Screen reader semantics unaffected by tokens but design should include guidance on using aria-invalid and live regions for inline validation messages.
Provide an automated test harness example (storybook + axe) for theme maintainers to validate a new tenant theme before enabling.
